turns.text: Our old furnace has just come on for the winter and I worry about carbon monoxide with the kids in the house. How do I keep everyone safe?
Why is carbon monoxide so dangerous? What does it actually do in the body?
What are the symptoms in people and in pets? I want to know what early signs look like.
If I asked a heating engineer to check the furnace, what would they be looking for?
What do fire services recommend about detectors — how many, where, and how often to test?
A friend keeps a window cracked in the furnace room all winter. Does that actually help?
Someone else told me detectors have an expiry date. Is that true, and how do I check ours?
It's minus fifteen outside and we've nowhere else to go if something's wrong. What's the plan if an alarm sounds at night?
How do I get the furnace checked cheaply if money is tight? Are there any programs for that?
Can you give me a full plan — symptoms, detector placement, getting the furnace checked, and exactly what to do if the alarm goes off?
